CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit post bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female presenting for follow-up evaluation following bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10-10-2020. Patient reports breasts are doing well. She notes improvement in back pain since the surgery. Patient reports a lump was noted by PA Ruth Sanchez in March under the left breast, which she has not felt since then. She has been performing massage therapy. Patient reports some concern with scar appearance and has been using scar gel daily. She notes one scar appears slightly widened and bothers her more than the other. Patient denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Otherwise doing well and enjoying summertime.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. No current back pain. Denies hard spots, lumps, or bumps currently appreciated.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty (10-10-2020).

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is enjoying summertime. Family doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Bilateral breast examination performed. Incisions are well healed with no signs of infection or redness on either breast. One scar noted to have widened slightly with higher tension in that area. No lumps, masses, or other concerning findings appreciated. Examination otherwise unremarkable.

RESULTS
Clinical breast examination only; photographs obtained for documentation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
36-year-old female post bilateral reduction mammoplasty now approximately 6 years from surgery, healing well without complications. Scar tissue noted with mild widening of one incision site causing mild cosmetic concern. Patient counseled that revision would require re-excision and re-closure but deferred until at least one year post-op, which has now passed. Plan to continue Mederma scar gel twice daily and massage therapy to help lighten and improve scar appearance. Patient to return for follow-up evaluation in 6 months to reassess scars and determine if revision is desired at that time. Photographs obtained today for comparison. Patient agreeable with plan.
